name: Four-stroke internal combustion engine (Otto cycle)
description: A heat engine in which fuel is burned inside the cylinder rather than (as with a steam engine) outside it. The four-stroke cycle — intake, compression, power, exhaust — was patented in 1862 by the French engineer Alphonse Beau de Rochas as a thermodynamic concept, but Nikolaus Otto built the first practical compressed-charge engine on this principle in May 1876, with a German patent granted in 1877. The Otto cycle is the propulsion ancestor of every petrol or diesel bus engine in history; Carl Benz used it in his 1885 Patent-Motorwagen and in the 1895 Netphen omnibuses, the first motorbuses in the world.

description_sources.quoted_text: Nikolaus Otto was a German engineer who developed the four-stroke internal-combustion engine, which offered the first practical alternative to the steam engine as a power source. Otto's innovation in creating a four-stroke piston cycle engine in 1876 marked a pivotal moment in engine design.

innovators.name: Nikolaus Otto
innovators.role: Built the first practical four-stroke compressed-charge internal-combustion engine, 1876
innovators.contribution: Solved the problem of progressive (rather than explosive) combustion via charge stratification — making the four-stroke principle commercially viable. Patent granted 1877.

sources.quoted_text: After 14 years of research and development, Otto succeeded in creating the compressed charge internal combustion engine on May 9, 1876, finding a way to layer the fuel mixture into the cylinder to cause the fuel to burn in a progressive, as opposed to explosive fashion.

innovators.name: Alphonse Beau de Rochas
innovators.role: Patented the four-stroke cycle as a thermodynamic concept, 1862
innovators.contribution: Theoretical formulation of the four-stroke cycle 14 years before Otto's working engine. Underrecognized because his patent didn't lead to a working machine and Otto's name attached to the cycle.

sources.quoted_text: Although Otto was the first to build an engine based upon this principle, the four-stroke cycle was patented in 1862 by the French engineer Alphonse Beau de Rochas, but it is commonly known as the Otto cycle.

key_dates.event: Beau de Rochas patents the four-stroke cycle as a concept.
key_dates.significance: Theoretical priority on the four-stroke cycle, but no working engine.

sources.quoted_text: the four-stroke cycle was patented in 1862 by the French engineer Alphonse Beau de Rochas

key_dates.event: Otto builds the first working compressed-charge four-stroke engine, 9 May.
key_dates.significance: Founding event of the modern internal-combustion engine industry.

sources.quoted_text: Otto succeeded in creating the compressed charge internal combustion engine on May 9, 1876

key_dates.event: Otto granted German patent for the four-stroke engine.
key_dates.significance: Patent later partially invalidated due to Beau de Rochas's prior art, but commercial dominance was already established.

sources.quoted_text: Otto was granted a patent for his four-stroke engine in 1877.
